questions.question: Give an example of a set that is bounded above, not below.
questions.solution_html:
• Solution:
  • a) Let T ={−s :s∈S}. Since S is bounded below, T is bounded above. . . . (2marks)
  • Let α = infS. Then α≤s for all s, so−α≥−s for all s,
  • hence−α is an upper bound for T . . . . (1marks)
  • For any upper bound M of T , M≥−s for all s,
  • so−M≤s for all s, hence−M is a lower bound for S, so−M≤α, . . . (2marks)
  • i.e., M≥−α.
  • Thus−α = supT .
  • So infS =α =− supT =− sup{−s :s∈S}. . . . (2marks)
  • b) For a ﬁnite set S ={x1,x 2, ,x n}, let M = max{x1, ,x n}. . . . (3marks)
  • By deﬁnition, M is an upper bound and M∈S,
  • hence M is the least upper bound, so sup S =M∈S. . . . (2marks) .

questions.question: Let be a nonempty subset of that is bounded above, and let be any number in . Define the set . Prove that .
questions.solution_html:
• Let S be a nonempty subset of R that is bounded above and let a be any number in
  • R. Deﬁne the set a +S ={a +s :s∈S}. Prove that sup(a +S) =a + supS. /[CO3]
  • Solution: Let u = supS. Then for all s∈S, s≤u, so a +s≤a +u. . . . (2marks)

  • so s≤v−a for all s. . . . (2marks)

  • Hence a +u is the least upper bound. . . . (2 marks)

questions.question: Solve for the real and imaginary parts of the function (a) and (b) . In each part, check whether the Cauchy–Riemann equations are satisfied or not.
questions.solution_html:
• Solve for the real and imaginary parts of the function (a) f(z) =iz + 2 and (b) f(z) =
  • x2y +i(xy2). In each part, check whether the Cauchy-Riemann equations are satisﬁed
  • or not. /[CO6]
  • Solution:
  • (a) f(z) =i(x +iy) + 2 =ix−y + 2 = (2−y) +ix.
  • So u(x,y ) = 2−y, v(x,y ) =x. . . . (1 mark)
  • Then ux = 0, uy =−1, vx = 1, vy = 0.
  • ux = 0 =vy and uy =−1 =−vx So CR equations are satisﬁed. . . . (2 marks)
  • (b) f(z) =x2y +ixy2. Then u =x2y, v =xy2.
  • Then ux = 2xy, uy =x2, vx =y2, vy = 2xy. . . . (1mark)
  • ux = 2xy =vy and uy =x2,−vx =−y2 =⇒
  • x2 =−y2 which holds only if x =y = 0.
  • CR not satisﬁed except at origin. . . . (2marks)

questions.question: Determine whether the function is harmonic.
questions.solution_html:
• Determine whether the function u(x,y ) = (x2−y2)2 is harmonic. /[CO7]
  • Solution: ux = 2(x2−y2)· 2x = 4x(x2−y2). . . . (1marks)
  • uxx = 4(x2−y2) + 4x(2x) = 12x2− 4y2. . . . (2marks)
  • uy = 2(x2−y2)· (−2y) =−4y(x2−y2). . . . (1mark)
  • uyy =−4(x2−y2) + (−4y)(−2y) =−4x2 + 4y2 + 8y2 =−4x2 + 12y2. . . . (2marks)
  • uxx +uyy = (12x2− 4y2) + (−4x2 + 12y2) = 8(x2 +y2),
  • which is not identically zero. So not harmonic. . . . (1mark)
  • (Total Mark should not exceed 6)
